India Tightens Foreign Funding Rules for NGOs Amidst Debate

The Indian government has notified new rules under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), imposing stricter conditions on non-governmental organizations receiving foreign funds. These changes include requirements for disclosing websites and social media during registration and restricting foreign nationals from serving as NGO functionaries. The amendments have sparked debate, with some outlets highlighting concerns about NGO freedom and democratic space, while others emphasize the government's intent to track funds and prevent misuse, particularly concerning religious conversion.
